newsitem.title: USA: American Intl Q4 life premium income up.
newsitem.headline: American Intl Q4 life premium income up.

text.p: American International Group Inc said premium income from its worldwide life insurance business rose 16.9 percent in the fourth quarter and in 1996, before the impact of foreign exchange.
Premium income rose 13.6 percent in the fourth quarter after foreign exchange to $2.47 billion and rose 11.7 percent to $8.98 billion for the year.
Operating income rose 19.5 percent in the quarter and 21.8 percent for the full year to a 1996 total of $1.29 billion, AIG said.
"All areas of life operations did very well in 1996," AIG chairman M.R. Greenberg said.
"The privatization of government pension programs in Latin America is accelerating and AIG is a leading player in this area," he said.

Shortly after year-end, AIG announced its new joint venture pension management company in Mexico and AIG said its growing overseas consumer finance businesses were augmented in 1996 with the purchase of Hong Kong based SPC Credit Ltd.
AIG said its financial services business had a strong year, with operating income up 25.4 percent to $524 million.
International Lease Finance Corporation had record operating income and significantly expanded its roster of airline customers, AIG said.
AIG Financial Products Corp. also reported a new high in operating income, as the market for its products and services was very strong.
AIG Trading Group Inc. also had a satisfactory year.
AIG said it made good progress in its infrastructure and direct equity funds.
The AIG-Brunswick Millennium Fund for Russia, the C.I.S. States and the Baltics, a direct equity investment fund that carries an OPIC principal guaranty, currently has over $288 million committed.

AIG announced in the fourth quarter the first closing of the AIG-GE Capital Latin American Infrastructure Fund, a private placement that will raise up to $1 billion for equity and convertible debt infrastructure investments in Latin America, the largest such fund ever raised.
Other such funds are in various stages of development and they should come to fruition in 1997, AIG said.
AIG said its equity in income of minority-owned insurance operations for the fourth quarter was $25.0 million, compared to $22.5 million in 1995.
Equity in income of minority-owned insurance operations amounted to $99.4 million in 1996, compared to $81.7 million in 1995.
